diagnosis.selected_diagnosis: The failed baseline is best explained by content-system imbalance: 90% promotional and 91.3% static output concentrated in two topics, reinforced by repetitive or missing CTAs. The issue is not that every promotion underperformed; rather, the mix left too little room for the educational, saveable, community, and retention-led formats that can build repeat demand.
counterevidence: Promotion median engagement remains close to the overall median, so promotion is not intrinsically ineffective.
Video median engagement (6.45%) is only slightly above post median (6.30%).
The community pillar has only two observations and is anecdotal, not proof of superiority.
diagnosis.outlier_caveat: The video mean is 11.13% but falls to 6.56% after removing one extreme video. This is directional evidence for testing video, not a causal claim.
diagnosis.decision: Shift from promotion-first repetition to a balanced, value-first test portfolio while preserving two commercial slots.

strategy.objective: Increase qualified saves, shares, profile actions, link-request comments, and repeat audience growth by making BudgetFitzz immediately useful.
strategy.audience_focus: Delhi NCR men aged about 18-30: college students, early-career professionals, and budget-sensitive style explorers (assumed context).
strategy.value_proposition: Practical Indian menswear decisions that look considered without overspending.
format_rules: Posts must deliver a complete takeaway on-frame.
Videos use a first-second hook, three meaningful scenes, readable captions, and a CTA end card.
hook_principles: Use numbers or tension only when the body pays it off.
Lead with the decision the audience needs to make.
cta_principles: Rotate save, share, vote, audit, and link-request intents.
Never use a wrong account handle.
strategy.posting_time_guidance: Treat historical timing as exploratory because cells are uneven. Start with 19:15-21:00 IST for interaction-led items and 12:30-13:15 IST for quick utility, then measure by comparable pillar/format.
strategy.visual_identity: Warm off-white editorial canvas, deep forest ink, electric lime utility highlights, coral commercial accents, modular cards, and original garment geometry.
video_retention_rules: Final CTA card remains visible for at least 1.5 seconds.
community_rules: Ask bounded questions people can answer quickly.
Respond using a reusable comment taxonomy: preference, fit problem, budget intent, and link intent.
strategy.promotion_limit: Maximum 2 of 7 items; every commercial item must teach a selection rule before presenting the product shortlist.
strategy.experimentation_plan: Run this as a seven-day pilot. Pre-register item-level primary KPI, compare only within format/pillar, retain raw outliers, and review median plus quartiles after the cycle.

evidence_linked_changes.interpretation: The brand asks for action more often than it earns attention through utility.
evidence_linked_changes.strategy_change: Cap promotional/value-first commercial items at 2 of 7; allocate 3 education and 2 community items.
evidence_linked_changes.expected_behavioural_effect: More saves, shares, repeat visits, and higher-quality comments.
evidence_linked_changes.success_metric: Pillar mix compliance; education median save rate; qualitative comment coding.
evidence_linked_changes.confidence_or_limitation: Strong concentration evidence; performance effect remains a forward test.

evidence_linked_changes.finding: Education median save rate is 0.522% vs promotion 0.232%.
evidence_linked_changes.interpretation: Useful explanations appear more saveable, though education has only 13 records.
evidence_linked_changes.strategy_change: Make the takeaway visible on-frame: formulas, checklists, comparisons, and avoidable mistakes.
evidence_linked_changes.expected_behavioural_effect: Users can understand and save the value without opening a long caption.
evidence_linked_changes.success_metric: Save rate target 0.45-0.70% on education posts.

evidence_linked_changes.finding: Posts are 91.3% of the baseline; video has n=13 and one extreme outlier.
evidence_linked_changes.interpretation: Video is under-tested and its mean is unreliable, but the format deserves controlled trials.
evidence_linked_changes.strategy_change: Use exactly two short videos with first-second hooks, 3-scene pacing, captions, and explicit end cards.
evidence_linked_changes.expected_behavioural_effect: Improved watch-through and more interpretable retention data.
evidence_linked_changes.success_metric: Retention proxy target 60-70% vs observed median 55.2%.
evidence_linked_changes.confidence_or_limitation: Directional; views are plays and not unique reach.

evidence_linked_changes.finding: Outfit Ideas and Budget Finds account for 66.7% of all records.
evidence_linked_changes.interpretation: Repeated topic territory limits discovery and audience learning.
evidence_linked_changes.strategy_change: Add wardrobe systems, fit diagnosis, colour voting, and wardrobe-audit topics while retaining familiar commercial anchors.
evidence_linked_changes.expected_behavioural_effect: Broader reasons to save, share, and return.
evidence_linked_changes.success_metric: No topic repeated more than twice in the seven-day cycle.
evidence_linked_changes.confidence_or_limitation: Concentration is certain; audience response must be tested.

evidence_linked_changes.finding: Fourteen CTAs are missing and two rows use @aristostyling.
evidence_linked_changes.interpretation: CTA and handle inconsistency reduce measurement clarity and brand trust.
evidence_linked_changes.strategy_change: Use one primary CTA per asset, rotate save/share/vote/link-request intents, and standardize @budgetfitzz.
evidence_linked_changes.expected_behavioural_effect: Cleaner attribution and less repetitive comment bait.
evidence_linked_changes.success_metric: 100% CTA coverage; 0 wrong-handle occurrences; at least 4 CTA styles across 7 items.
evidence_linked_changes.confidence_or_limitation: Direct quality-control fix; behavioral lift is a hypothesis.

plan.target_audience_segment: College students building a first versatile wardrobe
plan.hook: 3 pieces. 7 clean fits. No wardrobe haul.
plan.content_idea: Show one overshirt, one solid tee, and one dark trouser as a repeatable outfit system.
plan.visual_direction: Editorial capsule grid with original overshirt, tee, and trouser illustrations; lime numbered chips.
plan.caption_direction: Teach the formula, list swaps, and normalize repeating clothes.
plan.full_proposed_caption: A bigger wardrobe is not the same as a better wardrobe. Start with one textured overshirt, one solid tee and one dark straight-fit trouser. Wear the tee alone, layer the overshirt, switch the tuck, roll the sleeves, or swap in clean sneakers. That is already a week of useful combinations. Build systems before you buy more. Save this for your next wardrobe reset. Follow @budgetfitzz for practical style that respects your budget.
plan.cta: Save this 3-piece formula before your next purchase.
plan.baseline_insight: E01 + E03: education is scarce but has a 2.2x higher median save rate than promotion.
plan.reasoned_target_range: Save rate 0.50-0.70%; share rate 0.15-0.25% (targets, not observed results).

plan.target_audience_segment: Early-career men moving between commute, office, and evening plans
plan.hook: One overshirt. Three small fit moves in 10 seconds.
plan.content_idea: Show three visible adjustments to one forest textured overshirt: wear it open, button it lightly, then check the collar, cuff, and hem.
plan.visual_direction: One continuous all-photographic HF outfit clip with three timed editorial overlays and no illustrated garments or fictional location changes.
plan.caption_direction: Describe only the styling actions visible in the footage.
plan.full_proposed_caption: One overshirt, three small styling moves. First, wear it open so the cream tee stays visible and the layer feels relaxed. Second, button it lightly to create a cleaner front line without pulling the fabric. Third, check the collar, cuff and hem, then stop when the layer sits cleanly. This video shows one outfit in one setting, not three different occasions. Save the fit check and try it with a layer you already own. Follow @budgetfitzz for budget-first menswear systems.
plan.cta: Save the three fit moves and test them tonight.
plan.baseline_insight: E02 + E05 + E09: video is under-tested; mean performance is outlier-driven and median retention is about 55%.

plan.target_audience_segment: Followers who want quick feedback before a date or college event
plan.hook: Date night: A, B or C? Pick one.
plan.content_idea: Three original outfit colourways with a bounded vote and one-line styling rationale.
plan.visual_direction: Three side-by-side illustrated outfits labeled A/B/C with high-contrast vote footer.
plan.caption_direction: Invite a low-friction vote and ask respondents to name their setting.
plan.full_proposed_caption: You have one evening plan and three clean options. A: forest + cream for a warm, relaxed look. B: navy + stone for the safest smart-casual balance. C: burgundy + charcoal when you want more contrast. Comment A, B or C and tell us whether it is a café, dinner or college event. We will reply with the best shoe colour. Follow @budgetfitzz for useful outfit decisions, not random hauls.
plan.cta: Comment A, B or C plus the occasion.
plan.baseline_insight: E01 + E06: only two community items exist and topic territory is concentrated.
plan.reasoned_target_range: Qualified comments 1.2-2.0% of reach; share rate 0.15-0.25% (targets; community baseline is anecdotal).

plan.target_audience_segment: Price-sensitive college students with a fixed monthly clothing budget
plan.hook: ₹1,999 to look sharper: buy in this order.
plan.content_idea: Teach a prioritized basket: trouser first, solid tee second, overshirt third; show budget guardrails without claiming live prices.
plan.visual_direction: Receipt-inspired priority stack with original garment drawings and price-cap labels marked as illustrative targets.
plan.caption_direction: Give a decision rule before a link-request CTA; label price examples as budget targets.
plan.full_proposed_caption: If your upgrade budget is ₹1,999, do not split it across five weak pieces. Priority 1: one dark straight-fit trouser because it fixes the base of more outfits. Priority 2: one heavyweight solid tee in white, stone or black. Priority 3: only if money remains, add an overshirt. The displayed amounts are planning caps, not live product prices. Comment LINK only if you want a shortlist that follows this order. Follow @budgetfitzz for value-first recommendations.
plan.cta: Comment LINK for a shortlist built around the ₹1,999 cap.
plan.baseline_insight: E01 + E07: retain commercial intent but make it useful and replace repetitive link bait with one explicit, qualified CTA.
plan.reasoned_target_range: Link-request comments 0.8-1.5% of reach; save rate 0.35-0.55% (targets).

plan.target_audience_segment: Men whose outfits feel off despite buying current trends
plan.hook: A realistic fit check, from shoulder to shoe.
plan.content_idea: Use the visible balanced outfit to check the shoulder line, tee hem, and straight trouser line without claiming a before-and-after transformation.
plan.visual_direction: One continuous all-photographic HF full-body clip with four timed editorial overlays and no illustrated garments or unsupported corrections.
plan.caption_direction: Describe the fit visible in the footage and label it as a mirror checklist, not a transformation.
plan.full_proposed_caption: Use this as a mirror checklist, not a before-and-after. First, check that the sleeve seam sits near the shoulder and the tee lies smoothly without pulling. Second, check that the tee hem finishes close to the waistband with enough length to move and no excess bunching. Third, follow the trouser line down to a clean ankle and shoe. Read the whole silhouette before buying another piece. Save the three checks and test them on an outfit you already own. Follow @budgetfitzz for practical fit guidance.
plan.cta: Save the three visible fit checks and try them in the mirror.
plan.baseline_insight: E03 + E09: education is more saveable and current video retention leaves room for faster, explicit progression.

plan.target_audience_segment: First-job professionals choosing one versatile shoe
plan.hook: One sneaker budget? Rank by use, not hype.
plan.content_idea: Rank neutral court, retro runner, and chunky sneaker by versatility, comfort, and outfit compatibility without using brand logos.
plan.visual_direction: Original sneaker silhouettes on a three-row scorecard; coral highlights for trade-offs.
plan.caption_direction: Make the purchase framework the main value; product links are optional follow-up.
plan.full_proposed_caption: If you can buy one pair, rank the job before the hype. Neutral court sneaker: best for maximum outfit compatibility. Retro runner: best when walking comfort matters most. Chunky sneaker: strongest statement, but the least flexible with smart-casual trousers. Score your week across college or office, walking time and dress code before choosing. Comment SHOES if you want a no-logo shortlist by use case and budget. Follow @budgetfitzz for practical buying filters.
plan.cta: Comment SHOES with your budget and daily use case.
plan.baseline_insight: E06: Sneaker Review has only five records while two topics dominate; test adjacent commercial utility.
plan.reasoned_target_range: Qualified comments 0.7-1.3% of reach; save rate 0.35-0.55% (targets).

plan.target_audience_segment: Returning followers ready to reduce impulse purchases
plan.hook: Before Sunday checkout: pass this 5-point audit.
plan.content_idea: A saveable checklist asking whether a purchase creates three outfits, fits now, and replaces a real gap.
plan.visual_direction: Large checkboxes, lime pass/fail band, open space, and a comment prompt for the hardest rule.
plan.caption_direction: Close the week with reflection, audience input, and a measurable follow-up habit.
plan.full_proposed_caption: Before you check out, ask five things. Can I build three outfits with pieces I own? Does it fit my body now? Does it solve a real wardrobe gap? Will I wear it at least twice a month? Would I still want it without the discount label? Four yes answers means consider it. Three or fewer means wait 48 hours. Save the audit and comment the rule that saves you the most money. Follow @budgetfitzz for a smarter budget wardrobe.
plan.cta: Save the audit and comment your hardest rule.
plan.baseline_insight: E01 + E03 + E07: close with useful community interaction instead of another generic promotion or missing CTA.
plan.reasoned_target_range: Save rate 0.50-0.75%; qualified comments 0.8-1.5% of reach (targets).

prompts.prompt: Create a vertical editorial fashion photograph for BudgetFitzz. Subject: practical Indian menswear, realistic adult male model, wardrobe audit checklist. Scene: A saveable checklist asking whether a purchase creates three outfits, fits now, and replaces a real gap.. Visual direction: Large checkboxes, lime pass/fail band, open space, and a comment prompt for the hardest rule. Use natural garment texture, believable hands and anatomy, clean contemporary Indian home or city setting, soft daylight, restrained editorial composition, no brand logos, and leave safe negative space for the exact caption and CTA. The creative must support this approved hook: Before Sunday checkout: pass this 5-point audit.. Aspect ratio 4:5.

architecture.summary: The analytical pipeline processes the historical content dataset and generates metrics, evidence, strategy, content plans, creative assets, traces, and validation results. The packaging stage organizes approved outputs through a platform manifest. The Python backend serves the application and exposes only approved files. Frontend JavaScript reads those outputs and renders the latest project state without manually duplicating analytical values in the interface.

flow.label: Generated Outputs

flow.label: Platform Manifest
flow.description: A structured content index for current metrics, strategy, plan, assets, workflow, validation, and submission files.

flow.label: Python Backend
flow.description: ThreadingHTTPServer serves the app and approved outputs through allowlisted routes and a health endpoint.

flow.label: Frontend Application
flow.description: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fetch the generated manifest and render the current workspace.
